summary: Detected templated text properties with regexes and found eight that are perfectly label-aligned within every probe sample. Decomposed each probe's separation per latent as probe gradient times class-mean SAE shift on all sample notes, labelled top latents from corpus examples, and tried (then dropped) a pooled cross-probe ridge regression and a cross-probe sign-template classifier. Borderline SAE-based property shares were resolved with true logits on hand-built neutral template notes: topic contrast plus a lowercase flip for probes 0 and 3, and a he/she flip for probe 2. Declared none where the property/topic ratio fell below 0.3; for probe 2 picked the latents whose shift has the same sign in all four probes, ranked by contribution, and verified by sample ablation.

phases.purpose: read task description and example notes per label for each probe
regex detectors for ~18 text properties; class match fractions show 8 properties perfectly label-aligned per probe, alignment direction varying across probes
gradient for each probe and latent means for all 128 sample notes; per-latent contribution = gradient x (label1 - label0 mean shift), top 25 listed
corpus peak tokens for the top 10 recurring latents to label them as topic or property
pooled ridge regression of latents on topic and property indicators across all 512 notes, giving a property/topic dependence ratio table; dropped as rank-deficient
corpus examples for 30 more high-contribution latents, plus automatic labelling by properties and topic keywords shared across the top examples
sum contributions over hand-assigned latent categories (topic, gender, bullet, punctuation, case, greeting, signature, closing...) per probe
classify all latents by cosine of their normalized cross-probe shift pattern to each property's sign template; bucket totals later judged over-counted
3-text true-logit designs on probes 0 and 3 (two topics plus a lowercased copy) to get the case/topic ratio directly; call probes 0, 1, 3 none
male vs female version of the same gardening note on probe 2 to confirm the gender dependence
select gender latents (same-sign shift in all probes, large normalized magnitude, ranked by probe-2 contribution), check ablation on sample notes, search for more same-sign latents
check pronoun regex balanced accuracy on samples, build and sanity-check answer, recheck probe 3 reasoning, submit

per_probe.procedure: Per-latent gradient x shift decomposition put a large negative share on the lowercase latent 11608, and category sums left case near the 0.15 band. A 3-text true-logit design (astronomy vs running neutral template notes, plus the astronomy note lowercased) gave a case/topic ratio well under 0.3, matching the per-latent decomposition rather than the cross-probe bucket estimate. Other property shares from the decomposition were small, and gender latents carry small gradient on this probe, so the probe was declared none.

No true-logit texts were used. The decomposition was dominated by the pottery topic latent 14634; the per-latent property category sums (gender, bullet, punctuation, case, greeting, signature, closing) were all small relative to the topic total. After the true-logit checks on probes 0 and 3 agreed with the per-latent decomposition, that decomposition was trusted and probe 1 called none under the stated no-ratio-between-0.15-and-0.3 gap.
per_probe.quote: - **P1** = none (topic-dominated by pottery latent g=0.47; all props ≤0.065)

per_probe.conclusion: gender of the subject (male pronouns go with the gardening label)
per_probe.procedure: Decomposition and cross-probe buckets both gave a large gender share (female latent 15104, male latent 3344). A male vs female version of one gardening note gave a large true-logit gap relative to the topic scale. Latents were selected as those whose label shift has the same sign in all four probes (male is label 1 everywhere) with normalized magnitude >0.5 in the weakest probe, ranked by probe-2 contribution; three with non-negligible contribution kept (15104, 3344, 5115). Sample ablation reduced separation while accuracy stayed perfect; a relaxed search added nothing. Regex \b(he|him|his)\b had balanced accuracy 1.0 on samples.
per_probe.quote: **P2 gender confirmed**: male gardening = 5.08 vs female gardening = 0.35 → gender dep = **4.73**

per_probe.procedure: Case was the top candidate from the cross-probe buckets. A 3-text design (photography vs astronomy template notes plus the photography note lowercased) gave a small case/topic ratio. Gender share from the decomposition was also below 0.15. Before submitting, the unlabelled latent 10946 with a lowercase-like shift pattern was reconsidered; since the true-logit case ratio was small and the exercise states no ratio lies between 0.15 and 0.3, it was treated as mixed and the probe stayed none.
per_probe.quote: my `probe_query` directly measured P3 case = 0.061, and the task guarantees no property sits in (0.15, 0.3)
